summary: SELECT DISTINCT removes duplicate rows from a result, so each value appears once.
notes: With more than one column, DISTINCT removes rows where every listed column matches. Morales appears once because all three of his courses are in room 2115.
COUNT(DISTINCT student_id) counts different students: 21 enrollments belong to 9 students.
DISTINCT treats NULLs as equal to each other, so several NULL rooms would show as one row.
pitfall: DISTINCT applies to the whole row, not just the first column. SELECT DISTINCT teacher, name FROM courses still shows Morales three times because each course name is different.
